speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I see you are an adolescent presenting with delayed menarche, unusual physical features, and a history suggestive of bone fragility. To begin our assessment, how old are you, and do you have any specific family history of bone disorders or endocrine issues?

speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (specifically 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency) presenting as pseudohermaphroditism with hypertension and hypokalemia.

I have analyzed your history of ambiguous genitalia, severe acne, and bone fragility alongside your family's history of abnormal hair growth during pregnancy. These findings strongly suggest a steroidogenic enzyme defect rather than typical Turner syndrome.

REQUEST TEST: Plasma 17-OHP, 11-deoxycortisol, and cortisol; Serum renin and aldosterone; 24-hour urinary free cortisol.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound to assess gonadal development.
